core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aisha (Arabic عائشة, ʿĀʾishah) is an Arabic female name meaning “living” or “alive”. It is the name of Aisha bint Abi Bakr, the third wife of the Prophet Muhammad and one of the most important narrators of hadith, and it is very popular among Muslim women.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: ʿĀʾishah is the feminine active participle of the Arabic verb ʿāša, “to live”, so it literally means “she who lives” — “living, alive”.

etymology.morphology: Feminine active participle (fāʿila) of ʿāša, “to live”.
etymology.etymology_explanation: From the root ع ي ش (ʿ-y-š), “to live”.

origin.origin_explanation: Arabic; spread across the Muslim world in honour of Aisha bint Abi Bakr, with many local spellings (Ayesha, Ayşe, Aisyah, Aïcha).

religion.primary_association: Islamic — Aisha, wife of the Prophet
religion.religious_status: Name of a wife of the Prophet Muhammad (a Mother of the Believers)
religion.religious_explanation: Aisha bint Abi Bakr (c. 614–678) was the third and youngest wife of the Prophet Muhammad and daughter of Abu Bakr, the first caliph. She is credited with narrating over 2,000 hadiths and remained active in the Muslim community for 44 years after the Prophet's death.

prophetic_status.reference: Aisha bint Abi Bakr, wife of the Prophet Muhammad

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: In Sunni tradition Aisha is remembered as intelligent and scholarly, praised by early scholars for her knowledge of poetry, medicine and jurisprudence.
cultural_context.impact: The spelling Ayesha was briefly popular among English speakers after it appeared in H. Rider Haggard's novel She.

pronunciation.note: In South Asia usually AA-ee-sha; Turkish Ayşe is AY-sheh.

name_variants.variant_notes: Ayesha (South Asia, English), Ayşe (Turkish), Aisyah (Indonesian/Malay), Aïcha (French/Maghreb).

known_linguistic_history: Aisha bint Abi Bakr lived c. 614–678 CE and was politically active during the Rashidun Caliphate.
The 1990 US Census ranked Aisha 2,020th of 4,275 female names.
historical_context.historical_person_association: Aisha bint Abi Bakr (c. 614–678), wife of the Prophet Muhammad.

modern_usage.modern_context: Very popular among Muslim women; Ayesha and Aisha are both common spellings, and Ayşe is one of the most common Turkish female names.

faq.a: “Living” or “alive”, from the Arabic root ʿ-y-š, “to live”.
Aisha bint Abi Bakr (c. 614–678), the third and youngest wife of the Prophet Muhammad and daughter of Abu Bakr.

faq.q: Why is Aisha important in hadith?
faq.a: She is credited with narrating over 2,000 hadiths on the Prophet's life, law, ritual and theology.

faq.q: Aisha or Ayesha — which is correct?
faq.a: Both transliterate عائشة; Ayesha is common in South Asia and English.

islamic_naming_context.context: Given across the Muslim world in honour of Aisha bint Abi Bakr.
islamic_naming_context.interpretation: Chosen for its link with Aisha and for its meaning, “living”.
islamic_naming_context.important_distinction: The meaning “living” is lexical; the name's religious standing comes from Aisha bint Abi Bakr.

numerology.meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aisha total 2, associated with cooperation, balance and sensitivity. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.
